title: HUNTLEY-BYRNE v DALLISON 2021 LIMITED
text:
IN THE EMPLOYMENT RELATIONS AUTHORITY
WELLINGTON
I TE RATONGA AHUMANA TAIMAHI
TE WHANGANUI-A-TARA ROHE
[2026] NZERA 518
3379263
BETWEEN AUTO JOHN HUNTLEY-
BYRNE
Applicant
AND DALLISON 2021 LIMITED
Respondent
Member of Authority: Alyn Higgins
Representatives: Dave Cain, advocate for the Applicant
Kylie James for the Respondent
Submissions received: 3 July 2026 from the Applicant
20 July 2026 from the Respondent
Determination: 3 August 2026
COSTS DETERMINATION OF THE AUTHORITY
[1] In a determination dated 5 June 20261, the Authority issued a determination
finding the applicant, Auto John Huntly-Byrne had been unjustifiably dismissed from his
employment as a result of the actions of the respondent, Dallison 2021 Limited.
[2] In that determination, the parties were encouraged to resolve costs between them,
and the Authority made reference to its usual practice of applying the daily tariff to
determine costs.
1 Huntley-Byrne v Dallison 2021 Limited [2026] NZERA 354

[3] The parties have not been able to resolve costs between themselves and the
applicant has filed submissions as to costs for the Authority to determine.
The Parties’ Submissions
[4] The investigation meeting occupied most of a full day. At the end of the
investigation meeting leave was given for two further witnesses for the respondent to
appear via AVL, however this did not eventuate although tentative arrangements were
made.
[5] As the successful party Mr Huntley-Byrne’s representative seeks the full daily
tariff of $4,500 along with the $71.55 Authority filing fee. No uplift from the one day
daily tariff was sought.
[6] In their submissions the respondent acknowledges the Authority’s daily tariff
approach but submits that a reduction should be applied having regard to the Applicant’s
contributory conduct,2 the mixed outcome of the proceeding, the fact that aspects of the
determination remain under challenge, the Respondent’s financial circumstances, and the
unsupported allegations raised in paragraph 10 of the Applicant’s memorandum. In the
applicant’s submission on costs Mr Huntley-Byrne’s representative made reference to at
times unreasonable conduct but this was not detailed and I have not therefore taken it into
account.
[7] The respondent submits that a contribution of $2,500 toward the applicant’s costs
is appropriate.
Legal principles
[8] The power of the Authority to award costs is set out in clause 15 of Schedule 2 of
the Employment Relations Act 2000 (the Act). The principles and approach adopted by
the Authority in exercising this power are set out in the Authority’s Practice Direction
and the legal principles which underpin it.3
[9] These principles are:
2 In the substantive determination a 10% reduction in remedies for contribution was applied.
3 available at www.era.govt.nz/determinations/awarding-costs-remedies/#awarding-and-paying-costs-1

(a) An award of costs is discretionary.
(b) Costs will generally follow the event.
(c) The starting point for assessing costs is the notional daily tariff.
(d) The Authority then considers whether there are any relevant factors
which might led to increasing or decreasing the daily tariff. Factors
include:4
(i) costs awards in the Authority will be modest;
(ii) it is open to the Authority to consider whether all or any of the
parties’ costs were unnecessary or unreasonable;
(iii) costs are not to be used as a punishment or an expression of
disapproval of a party’s conduct although conduct which increases
costs unnecessarily can be considered in increasing the daily tariff;
and
(iv) the complexity of a matter may justify an increase in the daily tariff.
Application
[10] I have genuinely considered the grounds put forward by the Respondent in support
of a reduced costs award. The contributory conduct by the applicant was addressed (as it
was required to be) in the substantive determination and a reduction of remedies was
applied accordingly. Further, and as noted above, costs are not to be used as an expression
of disapproval of a party’s conduct.
[11] Similarly, any challenge to the substantive determination is not a consideration as
far as a costs award is concerned.
[12] A costs award is concerned with the time and conduct of the investigation
meeting, not the substantive issues dealt with in the substantive determination or any
further proceedings thereafter.
[13] The applicant was substantively successful, costs should follow the event and the
successful applicant is entitled to a contribution to their costs. This is the starting point.
4 JCE v The Chief Executive of the Department of Corrections [2018] NZERA 175 at [4]

[14] In the present case, the applicant was the successful party. Although the
respondent has referred to a “mixed outcome” as a reason for reducing costs this is still a
success overall.
[15] In regard to the reference to the Respondent’s financial circumstances, the
Authority’s approach to costs is set out on the Authority’s website.5 This was also
included in the substantive determination6 and provides the following:
We may reduce the costs an unsuccessful party needs to pay if they can prove that paying
normal costs would cause considerable hardship. They will need to file affidavit evidence
with us about their financial and personal situation.
[16] No such affidavit evidence of considerable hardship was provided in the
Respondent’s submissions.
[17] The approach to costs is focused on access to justice and modest costs awards.
The daily tariff has been put in place to give parties some certainty of what the costs
consequences of pursuing a claim, or losing a claim, are likely to be.
[18] Standing back and considering the substantive outcome for the reasons outlined I
do not consider that there is any reason to depart from the one day daily tariff rate in this
case.
Outcome
[19] Having considered the submissions as to costs, within 28 days of the date of this
determination, Dallison 2021 Limited is ordered to pay Auto John Huntly-Byrne the sum
of $4,500 as a contribution towards costs incurred. Mr Huntly-Byrne is also entitled to
be reimbursed the Authority’s filing fee ($71.55).
[20] Orders are made accordingly.
Alyn Higgins
Member of the Employment Relations Authority
